newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma widens crackdown on anti-government unrest.
newsitem.headline: Burma widens crackdown on anti-government unrest.

text.p: Burma's military rulers have widened their crackdown on anti-government unrest, tightening security in the capital Rangoon and arresting members of the country's opposition party, dissident figures said on Thursday.
National League for Democracy (NLD) deputy leader Tin Oo said some 28 members had been arrested in the past five days, 13 of them from the NLD youth wing and one NLD politician.
The NLD won a general election in 1990 that was not recognised by the ruling military government.

A spokesman for the government, facing the most serious protests since it crushed a 1988 democracy uprising, said it would maintain restrictions on opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's movements as long as the student unrest continued.
When asked how long the restrictions would be in force, he told Reuters: "As long as the situation still does not go back to normal."
He said the Nobel laureate and NLD leader had been asked to temporarily stay at home for her own safety.
The NLD's Tin Oo said the NLD parliamentarian was detained for nearly one day before his release on Wednesday. Military spokesmen were not immediately available to comment.

The military, apparently responding to rumours university students may attempt a demonstration in a square in front of city hall in Rangoon's business district, placed about 20 truckloads of soldiers and riot police at the site on Thursday.
Protesters, however, failed to show up at the square, which was fronted by military trucks, but no soldiers.

"Both the government and students are running against time. The authorities are using tough measures to try to stifle protests as quickly as possible while students are struggling to keep the momentum of their activities," a Rangoon-based diplomat said.
The NLD has denied any link to the student protests.

Tin Oo told Reuters the arrested NLD members were onlookers during protests last week by over 500 students of the Yangon University at a road junction and said they did not participate in the demonstration which was dispersed by force on Saturday.

He said six of the arrested had been released after interrogation. "They were warned before their release not to talk about their arrest and questioning or they would be violating the Government Secrets Act," Tin Oo said.

The NLD leader said government intelligence officers picked up the NLD members near the house of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi after their faces matched those in pictures taken by government agents near the scene of protests on Friday.

The government had said soldiers and police briefly detained 264 students and sympathisers from the protests which, along with another demonstration on December 2, was among the biggest seen in Rangoon since the 1988 pro-democracy uprisings.
Security was tight on Thursday. The Sule Pagoda, a landmark in the central district adjoining the square, was closed, apparently as part of security measures.
Tin Oo said those NLD members still being detained had been sent to the maximum security Insein prison to await trials.
The government has also postponed the Rangoon Mayor Marathon, which had been scheduled for Saturday.

The annual event, which attracts thousands of Burmese and foreign participants, was to be run on thoroughfares that have since been blockaded bordering the closed Yangon University and the Yangon Institute of Technology.
In the latest protests demanding more politicial freedom, more than 860 people were detained and later freed by the government.
